To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
zeolite can increase the physical and chemical stability of the magnesium potassium phosphate compound, which can be used for the immobilization of high-level nuclear waste.
the addition of zeolite (up to 28.6%) to the composition of magnesium potassium phosphate (MgKPO4∙6H2O) compound increases its mechanical strength, thermal resistance, and hydrolytical stability.
the addition of natural zeolite to MKP compound for the immobilization of high-level radioactive waste improves its physical, mechanical and chemical properties.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of new materials for the immobilization of high-level nuclear wastes, and the possibility of using natural zeolite from the Sokyrnytsya deposits as an additive to increase the mechanical and thermal stability of the compound.
the development of new materials for the solidification of high-level radioactive waste (HLW).
the development of new materials for the immobilization of high-level waste.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the use of the Sokyrnytsya zeolite in the composition of the magnesium potassium phosphate compound for the immobilization of high-level waste allows us to increase its physical and chemical stability and to obtain a material suitable for use in the Russian Federation.
the zeolite can be used as an additive to the MKP compound for the immobilization of HLW.

the use of the natural zeolite (the Sokyrnytsya deposits) as a filler for the immobilization of high-level waste (in the form of a magnesium potassium phosphate compound) allows one to increase the mechanical resistance of the compound, to reduce the leaching rate, and to increase the hydrolytic stability of the compound.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the addition of zeolite in the amount of 28.6% to the MKP compound increases its mechanical, thermal and hydrolytic stability.
the developed MKP compound with zeolite can be used to immobilize HLW.
the addition of zeolite in the composition of the magnesium potassium phosphate compound allows to obtain the compound with high compressive strength and high hydrolytic stability.
The main takeaway from our work is that
zeolite is an effective additive to the composition of a compound based on magnesium potassium phosphate, which improves its physicochemical properties.
the addition of zeolite from the Sokyrnytsya deposits to the MKP compound can increase the resistance of the compound to mechanical and hydrolytic effects.
zeolite can significantly improve the properties of a magnesium potassium phosphate compound for the immobilization of HLW, and it is a promising material for the production of immobilized HLW.
